findings.title: Denial cache is consulted before the permission cache, so a stale denial overrides fresher cached grants
findings.body: In Check, the denial cache is checked first (lines 116-121) and returns Allowed=false immediately, before the cached permission set is consulted (line 123). Denial entries live for shortCacheTTL (30s) and are never invalidated. Consider: (1) a user is denied resource A after a DB requery, so a denial entry for A is cached; (2) the user is then granted A in the DB; (3) any other cache miss for the same user+action re-queries the DB and refreshes permCache, which now includes A; (4) a new Check for A hits the stale denial entry and returns false even though the server's own fresh permCache would allow it. This reintroduces the exact 'user can't access a resource they were just granted' problem this PR is meant to fix, for up to 30s after any denial. Checking the cached permissions first (allow on positive evidence, then consult the denial cache for the fast-deny path) would avoid contradicting fresher cached grants while keeping the denial fast path.

findings.title: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates name/parent with underscores, which they can themselves contain, allowing key collisions
findings.body: The key is built as namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent with no escaping. Dashboard and folder UIDs may contain underscores, so two different (name, parent) pairs can produce the same key: e.g. (name="dash_1", parent="x") and (name="dash", parent="1_x") both yield "..._dash_1_x". A denial cached for one resource would then incorrectly deny a different resource/parent combination for up to the 30s TTL. Use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or otherwise unambiguously encode the fields.

findings.title: Denial-precedence test caches a non-allowing permission, so it doesn't prove the denial cache wins over cached grants
findings.body: In the subtest "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry", the comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code stores map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} in permCache. With a false value the cached permissions would deny the request anyway, so the test would still pass if the denial-cache branch in Check were broken or removed. The cached scope should be set to true so the test actually verifies that a denial entry takes precedence over an allowing cached permission set.
